Figure 3: B5 ARI on synthetic composites versus real squashed diffs, matched by observed commit count k. B5 receives the true k for both sides; the shaded band highlights the ARI gap.

Figure 1: Overview of retrospective commit-history reconstruction. Given a base repository snapshot and a squashed multi-commit diff, the task is to group hunks into commits and materialize a replayable history. Evaluation separates structural replay validity, reference-based grouping quality, and selective-revert failure containment.

Figure 6: An anonymized representative reconstruction case. The squashed diff interleaves a timeout bug fix, an option-parser refactor, and release metadata. A maintainable history must split same-file hunks, group cross-file hunks, and keep support hunks with the change intent they support.

Figure 2: Main grouping results on 800 natural retrospective episodes. Points report ARI against the observed developer decomposition; colors distinguish diagnostic baselines, model-agent setups, and DACE-augmented runs.
